nodes.name: CV electrodeposition of NiCoMnFe-P
nodes.procedure: NiCoMnFe-based high-entropy phosphide (NiCoMnFe–P) on stable Ti mesh by CV electrodeposition from 0.2 to -1.2 V vs. SCE for 3 cycles.
nodes.source_text: Allam’s group reported NiCoMnFe-based high-entropy phosphide (NiCoMnFe–P) on stable Ti mesh by CV electrodeposition from 0.2 to - 1.2 V vs. SCE for 3 cycles [69].

nodes.name: NiMoPSO NCAs/NF
aliases: high-chaos nickel molybdenum phosphorus sulfide oxides on nickel foam

nodes.name: Potentiostatic electrodeposition of NiMoPSO
nodes.procedure: High-chaos nickel molybdenum phosphorus sulfide oxides on nickel foam (NiMoPSO NCAs/NF) by potentiostatic electrodeposition at -0.6 V for 900 s in two-electrode system.
nodes.source_text: Chen’s group has electrodeposited high-chaos nickel molybdenum phosphorus sulfide oxides on nickel foam (NiMoPSO NCAs/NF) by potentiostatic electrodeposition at - 0.6 V for 900 s in two-electrode system (Fig. 5a) [70].

nodes.name: Galvanostatic electrodeposition of NFCCW-HEA
nodes.procedure: Nanoporous Ni-Fe-Cu-Co-W high-entropy alloy (NFCCW-HEA) by galvanostatic electrodeposition at a current density of 100 mA·cm⁻².
nodes.source_text: Bian et al. [72] have prepared nanoporous Ni-Fe-Cu-Co-W high-entropy alloy (NFCCW-HEA) for efficient OER electrocatalysis by galvanostatic electrodeposition at a current density of 100 mA·cm⁻².

nodes.name: Cathodic plasma electrodeposition of FeCoNiMnCu HEA
nodes.procedure: Quinary Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Cu high-entropy alloy (FeCoNiMnCu HEA) by cathodic plasma electrodeposition technique at the voltage of 130 V for 3 min with 70% duty cycle.
nodes.source_text: Huang et al. [73] have synthesized quinary Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Cu high-entropy alloy (FeCo-NiMnCu HEA) by cathodic plasma electrodeposition technique at the voltage of 130 V for 3 min with 70% duty cycle.

nodes.name: Potentiostatic electrodeposition of NiFeCoMnAl oxide
nodes.procedure: Nanoporous NiFeCoMnAl oxide on carbon fiber by first potentiostatic electrodeposition in DMSO at -2.8 V vs. SCE and then subsequent alkaline etching.
nodes.source_text: Han et al. [74] have reported nanoporous NiFeCoMnAl oxide on carbon fiber by first potentiostatic electrodeposition in DMSO at -2.8 V vs. SCE and then subsequent alkaline etching (Fig. 7a).

nodes.name: FeCoNiMnOOH/NF
aliases: high-entropy FeCoNiMn (oxy)hydroxide nanosheet on nickel foam

nodes.name: Potentiostatic electrodeposition of FeCoNiMnOOH
nodes.procedure: High-entropy FeCoNiMnOOH nanosheet on nickel foam (FeCoNiMnOOH/NF) electrocatalyst by potentiostatic electrodeposition at -1.0 V vs. SCE.
nodes.source_text: He et al. [76] reported high-entropy FeCoNiMnOOH nanosheet on nickel foam (FeCo-NiMnOOH/NF) electrocatalyst by potentiostatic electrodeposition at - 1.0 V vs. SCE (Fig. 8a).

nodes.name: Potentiostatic electrodeposition of FeCoNiMnCuOOH
nodes.procedure: High-entropy (oxy)hydroxide (FeCoNiMnCuOOH-20) nanosheets by potentiostatic electrodeposition at -1.0 V vs. SCE for 20 min.
nodes.source_text: Hu’s group has synthesized high-entropy (oxy)hydroxide (FeCoNiMnCuOOH-20) nanosheets by potentiostatic electrodeposition at - 1.0 V vs. SCE for 20 min [77].

nodes.name: Pulse electrodeposition of H-FeCoNiCuMo
nodes.procedure: Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Mo-based high-entropy alloy (H-FeCoNiCuMo) by pulse current density at -4000 mA·cm⁻² with a duty cycle of 0.2 s (on)/0.8 s (off) for 3000 cycles.
nodes.source_text: Lu’s group has reported Fe-Co-Ni-Cu-Mo-based high-entropy alloy (H-FeCoNiCuMo) by pulse current density at - 4000 mA·cm⁻² with a duty cycle of 0.2 s (on)/0.8 s (off) for 3000 cycles (Fig. 9a, b) [84].

nodes.name: Pulse electrodeposition of H-FeCoNiMnW
nodes.procedure: Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-W-based high-entropy alloy (H-FeCoNiMnW) by pulse current electrodeposition at 8000 mA·cm⁻² with an on/off cycle of 0.2/0.8 s for 3000 cycles.
nodes.source_text: Lu’s group has reported another research on Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-W-based high-entropy alloy (H-FeCoNiMnW) by pulse current electrodeposition at 8000 mA·cm⁻² with an on/off cycle of 0.2/0.8 s for 3000 cycles [85].

nodes.name: Nanodroplet-mediated electrodeposition of CoFeLaNiPt HEMG-NP
nodes.procedure: Co-Fe-La-Ni-Pt-based high-entropy metallic glass nanoparticles (CoFeLaNiPt HEMG-NP) by nanodroplet-mediated electrodeposition. The water nanodroplets containing metal salt precursors are suspended in dichloroethane with the assistance of tetrabutylammonium perchlorate surfactant. CoFeLaNiPt HEMG-NP (diameter < 500 nm) is obtained by an electro-shock of 100 ms.
nodes.source_text: Glasscott et al. [86] have synthesized Co-Fe-La-Ni-Pt-based high-entropy metallic glass nanoparticles (CoFeLaNiPt HEMG-NP) by nanodroplet-mediated electrodeposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows no change between as-prepared and post-stability test NiCoMnFe-P, indicating structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, there was no change in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum between the as-prepared and long-term tested electrocatalyst, indicating the structure stability of NiCoMnFe–P.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD analysis indicates NiMoPSO is a high-chaos compound composed of NiP₂, NiS₂, MoP₂, MoS₂, and MoO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD and HRTEM analysis indicate that NiMoPSO is a high-chaos compound of NiP₂, NiS₂, MoP₂, MoS₂ and MoO₃ (Fig. 5c, d).

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing lattice fringes
3D representation of multi-element atomic cluster showing lattice distortion

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows hierarchical nanocolumn array morphology with large surface area for NiMoPSO NCAs/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology structure of NiMoPSO NCAs/NF is hierarchical nanocolumn array with the large surface area (Fig. 5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-SEM image after stability test shows almost no morphology changes for NiMoPSO NCAs/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The post-scanning electron microscope (SEM) image of NiMoPSO after the stability test has almost no changes, further implying the strong stability of NiMoPSO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-Raman spectra show formation of Ni oxide and MoO₄²⁻ on NiMoPSO surface after HER stability test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the post-Raman spectra reveal the formation of Ni oxide and MoO₄²⁻, indicating the surface construction of NiMoPSO during the HER process.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NFCCW-HEA has face-centered cubic (FCC) phase with small quantity of amorphous phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase of the NFCCW-HEA is face-centered cubic (FCC) with a small quantity of amorphous phase, due to the sluggish diffusion effect and slow crystal nucleation (Fig. 6c, d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms FCC phase of FeCoNiMnCu HEA with severe lattice distortion showing dislocations and stacking faults in (11-1̄) lattice plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase of FeCoNiMnCu HEA is also confirmed as FCC phase by HRTEM and XRD measurements (Fig. 6i–k). Severe lattice distortion exists in FeCoNiMnCu FCC structure for the observation of dislocations and stacking faults in the (11-1̄) lattice plane (Fig. 6j).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals nanoparticle morphology of FeCoNiMnCu HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscope (TEM) image reveals the nanoparticle morphology of FeCoNiMnCu HEA (Fig. 6h).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms amorphous structure of NiFeCoMnAl oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase of NiFeCoMnAl oxide is confirmed as amorphous structure by TEM measurement (Fig. 7b).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS spectra (Ni 2p, Fe 2p, Co 2p, Mn 2p) show Mn donates electrons to Ni, Co, Fe due to low electronegativity, creating electron-rich active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Because of the low electronegativity of Mn, Mn could donate electron to Ni, Co, Fe, resulting in the electron-rich Ni, Co, Fe atoms (Fig. 7c–f).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows formation of γ-NiOOH (475 cm⁻¹) and β-NiOOH (555 cm⁻¹) under OER potentials, with high β-NiOOH content due to Mn-Ni electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman analysis reveals the self-construction of γ-NiOOH (475 cm⁻¹) and β-NiOOH (555 cm⁻¹) intermediates under applied OER potentials (Fig. 7j).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows FeCoNiMnOOH has amorphous structure with poor crystallinity of (Fe₀.₆₇Ni₀.₃₃)OOH, (Fe₀.₆₇Mn₀.₃₃)OOH, and (Fe₀.₆₇Co₀.₃₃)OOH phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of FeCoNiMnOOH is characterized as amorphous structure with poor crystals of (Fe₀.₆₇Ni₀.₃₃)OOH, (Fe₀.₆₇Mn₀.₃₃)OOH and (Fe₀.₆₇Co₀.₃₃)OOH (Fig. 8b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms amorphous nanosheet structure of FeCoNiMnOOH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of FeCoNiMnOOH is characterized as amorphous structure with poor crystals of (Fe₀.₆₇Ni₀.₃₃)OOH, (Fe₀.₆₇Mn₀.₃₃)OOH and (Fe₀.₆₇Co₀.₃₃)OOH (Fig. 8b, c).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows H-FeCoNiCuMo composition Fe:Co:Ni:Cu:Mo = 16.1:21.5:21.7:20.2:20.5 atomic ratios.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) verifies that the molecular atomic ratios of Fe: Co: Ni: Cu: Mo are 16.1: 21.5: 21.7: 20.2: 20.5, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms H-FeCoNiCuMo has solid solution FCC phase structure without phase separation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of H-FeCoNiCuMo is the solid solution FCC phase without any phase separation (Fig. 9c, d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows uniform atomic distribution in H-FeCoNiCuMo FCC phase with consistent lattice constant ~0.36 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The five components are also found to be uniformly distributed in FCC phase for the identical lattice constant ~0.36 nm measured by HRTEM and XRD analysis as well as Vegard's rule calculation (Fig. 9c, d).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows no changes in oscillation frequencies/amplitudes of Ni, Fe, Mo during HER; increased coordination numbers for Co, Cu in alkaline HER RDS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy testifies that there are no changes of oscillation frequencies and amplitudes of Ni, Fe and Mo elements with HER reduction potentials increasing (Fig. 9j–l).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows formation of FeOOH, CoOOH, NiOOH, Cu(III)O₂⁻, and MoO₂ active species on H-FeCoNiCuMo.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals that FeOOH, CoOOH, NiOOH, Cu(III)O₂⁻ and MoO₂ are formed during the OER process (Fig. 9o), which are well-known active species for OER electrocatalysts.
